name: Button
purpose: The site's one solid control. It is a promise to go somewhere on this site, or to start something here.
useFor: In-site destinations (368 Dinos), and the About page's profile links.
dontUseFor: Leaving the site from inside a case-study panel. That is SiteLink, which borrows the Stamp's pill so a panel gains a control without gaining a second visual language.
anatomy: Ink border 2.5px, paper fill, hard 4px offset shadow, body font at 700. Hover lifts 1px and the shadow grows to 6px; press drops 3px and the shadow collapses to 1px, so the button meets the paper.
html: GitHubPlay it →hoverpressed

name: SiteLink
purpose: A live link out of the site, worn as the Stamp's pill so it costs the panel no new language.
useFor: Only for leaving the site. It lives in the panel footer next to the built-with line.
dontUseFor: In-site navigation, which keeps the solid Button because it is a different promise. Never rotate it: a tilted pill reads as a Stamp.
anatomy: Mono caps at 0.72rem, 2px ink border, full radius, no fill. Hover fills with ink and lifts 1px.
html: b43.ai →unscary.ai →hover →

name: CopyLine
purpose: An install command a visitor can take: the command as selectable mono text, with an ink Copy half.
useFor: Commands on the skills page, one per skill plus the install-everything line at the top. The prompt variant carries the line you paste into Claude Code.
dontUseFor: Prose. Never inside a sticky panel: it has no place in their height budget.
anatomy: 2.5px ink frame with the Button's 4px resting shadow. Mono command at 0.85rem, wrapping at its spaces. The Copy half is mono caps on ink, 9ch wide so Copy and Copied never shift the line. Hidden without JS; the command stays selectable.
html:
npx skills add Schubaru/skills --skill ui-surgeon
npx skills add Schubaru/skills

name: Stamp
purpose: The graded mark on a case study: what state the work is actually in.
useFor: One per panel, top right of the study head. Short and factual: IN PRODUCTION, iOS · v1, SHIPPED.
dontUseFor: Anything that can be clicked. It is a mark, not a control, and its rotation is what says so.
anatomy: Mono caps at 0.72rem, 2px ink border, full radius, rotated 6 degrees. Absolutely positioned in the study head; it becomes static and inline below 900px.
html: IN PRODUCTIONiOS · v1SHIPPED

name: Panel
purpose: The case-study card: a sheet of paper laid on the paper, holding one piece of work end to end.
useFor: One per case study. It fills the lane between the red margin line and the monkey's gutter, and it is capped so it can never grow into either.
dontUseFor: Short content. A panel that is not carrying a head, three beats, shots and a built-with line is just a bordered box.
anatomy: Head (h2 + deck + Stamp), body (TapedShot in the 8fr column, Beats in the 5fr column), footer (built-with line + SiteLinks). Ink border 2.5px, hard 8px offset shadow, fluid padding 24-56px.
html:
Wordsword

A dictionary that keeps your words.

iOS · v1

What it is

The head, one beat and the built-with line, with the shots left out so the frame itself is visible.

SwiftUI · Claude Codewordsword.app →

name: Beat
purpose: One step of the case study's argument: what it is, then why it works this way, then my role.
useFor: Exactly three per panel, in that order. The middle one names the decision and the thing it rejected; the third is first person and picks one hard part.
dontUseFor: A stack list. The built-with line already carries the stack. And never more than three: only one beat is visible at a time, so a fourth is a beat nobody reads.
anatomy: Mono caps heading at 0.76rem in ink-soft, then a paragraph at a 48ch measure. The heading sits BELOW the body in the hierarchy because it is a signpost, not a headline.
html:
What it is

A tiny browser puzzle. Match three dinos to rescue them; let the board fill and it is an EXTINCTION EVENT.

Why it works this way

A five-second game has no business asking for an install, an account, or a tutorial.

My role

Three files. Zero dependencies. No build step. Every dino is hand-inlined SVG.

name: TapedShot
purpose: Real screenshots taped onto the paper. The evidence, and the reason the shots get the wide column.
useFor: One arrangement per case study, and they must stay distinct: two identical fans back to back read as a template rather than a hand.
dontUseFor: Mockups, device frames, or anything that is not the software actually running.
anatomy: A figure rotated -1.6deg holding absolutely positioned screens, each with a 2.5px ink border, plus two masking-tape SVGs. Three arrangements: phone-shot is a dealt deck, stack-shot is a centre-forward trio, wide-shot is one letterboxed dashboard with close-ups taped over it.
html:
phone-shot · a dealt deck

stack-shot · centre forward

wide-shot · taped close-ups

name: DemoReel
purpose: The same taped frame, but a silent looping video of the thing actually running.
useFor: When the work is motion and a still cannot carry it. 368 Dinos plays bare; the don-star card on /skills wears the controls variant.
dontUseFor: Anything a screenshot already proves. A reel costs bandwidth and attention that a still does not.
anatomy: A video inside a .shot with preload none and a real screenshot as poster, so it costs nothing until it is nearly on screen and a reduced-motion visitor keeps a true still. Autoplay lives in JS, never in the markup: that is what keeps the motion contract in one place. The controls variant adds .reel on the figure and a .reel-ctl pair of .reel-btn icon buttons (Pause/Play, Expand); JS reveals them and builds the enlarged dialog (.reel-box) from the same video.
html: Shown at its poster frame, which is exactly what a reduced-motion visitor gets.

name: Doodle
purpose: Hand-authored inline SVG in one ink, one weight. The illustration system, and the site's whole hand.
useFor: Only the cast: the knight in the wordmark (and, with his challenger, on Wordsword's built-with line), the monkey in the right lane, the diver in the case-study transition, and the masking tape. Each one has a job.
dontUseFor: Scattered marks. Skulls, stars, sparks, bolts, crowns, flames, hearts and horns are all gone: decoration was the thing making the page loud. If a new mark cannot name its job, it does not go on the page.
anatomy: Stroke width 2.6 at a 100-unit viewBox (4.2 for small doodles like the wordmark knight), round caps and joins, no fill, currentColor so the mark inherits ink. Every path carries pathLength=1 so it can draw itself in on scroll entry; reduced motion gets it pre-drawn.

name: Annotation
purpose: A margin note in the reader's own hand: small, soft, slightly off-axis.
useFor: Labelling something the layout cannot say by itself, like the diver strip's “going deeper…”.
dontUseFor: Anything load-bearing. If the page falls over without the annotation, it is body copy and should look like it.
anatomy: 0.95rem at weight 500 in ink-soft, line-height 1.3, rotated 2-4 degrees when it sits in the margin.
html:
going deeper…

rotated, the way it sits in the margin

name: TopNav
purpose: The sticky header: the wordmark with the knight standing guard in front of it, and two destinations: Skills and The Arbiter.
useFor: One per page, always. It is the only chrome the site has.
dontUseFor: Growing. Its height is what every sticky panel's height budget is measured off, which is why the knight is taken out of flow and overhangs into the nav's padding.
anatomy: Wordmark at 700/1.4rem with the knight absolutely positioned in a 41px lane (30px below 640px), then three nav links with an ink underline on hover. Paper at 88 percent with a 6px backdrop blur, 2px ink bottom border.
html:
N00B Labs™
WorkThe ArbiterAbout

name: SkipLink
purpose: The first thing in the tab order: a way straight to the work.
useFor: Once, as the first element in the body. It is off-screen until focused.
dontUseFor: Anything else. There is one skip target on this site and it is the work.
anatomy: Absolutely positioned off-screen at left -999px; focus brings it to left 8px. Ink fill, paper text, 700 weight.
html: Skip to the workshown in its focused state; until then it sits at left:-999px

name: Chat
purpose: The Arbiter's mini chat on the black page: a hand-authored dialogue tree of 309 nodes and 927 replies.
useFor: Once, in the Arbiter section. Three replies per turn; slots one and two stay in the bit, slot three turns philosophical.
dontUseFor: A general chat component. There is no exit here: every reply opens three more, and the conversation outlasting the visitor is the character.
anatomy: A log (role=log, aria-live=polite, focusable) over a group of three ChatButtons. The wall reply is marked in margin-red so you can see it coming. On the night surface, so every ink value inverts to night-ink.
html:
Speak.

What do you do all day?

I wait for a webhook.

name: ChatButton
purpose: One of the Arbiter's three replies. The only control that lives on the night surface.
useFor: Always three at a time, inside Chat. The --rule modifier marks a reply that reaches the wall.
dontUseFor: Anywhere on paper. It is built for the black page and its shadow colour assumes it.
anatomy: Night-ink border and text, hard offset shadow in soft ink at 70 percent, growing on hover and collapsing to 1px on press. The rule modifier swaps the shadow to margin-red. Below 560px the three stack full width, because three long replies side by side read as confetti.

name: Colophon
purpose: The last word: how the site was made, and the copyright.
useFor: Once, at the end of the page. Two short paragraphs, mono.
dontUseFor: Navigation. The nav is at the top and the page is one scroll; a link farm down here would be a second nav nobody asked for.
anatomy: Mono at 0.8rem in ink-soft, centred under a top border, sitting on the rule grid like everything else.
html:
Hand-drawn SVG · vanilla HTML/CSS/JS · no framework · no build step. The paper is one CSS gradient.
